issues.legal_issue: A member’s right to occupy a flat owned by a cooperative housing society is attachable and saleable in execution of a decree when the governing law does not prohibit transfer of that right.
material_facts: The proceeding was execution of a money decree against a judgment-debtor who had the beneficial right to occupy a flat owned by a cooperative housing society.
The flat was held in the names of the judgment-debtor’s brother and his wife on the judgment-debtor’s behalf.
The society’s rules and bye-laws restricted transfers but did not make a transfer of the occupancy right void, and a qualified transferee could apply for membership.
The society did not object to attachment and sale of the occupancy right.
issues.conclusion: The right to occupy the flat was a species of property that could be attached and sold in execution; the statutory protection for a member’s share or interest in the society’s capital did not extend to that right.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 29 and 31 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act, 1960 distinguish a member’s interest in the capital of a society from an interest in its property; section 31 protects the former, not the right to occupy a flat. Section 29, Rule 24 of the Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Rules, 1961, and Bye-law 9 permit transfer subject to the applicable membership requirements. Bye-law 71D’s consent restriction does not make a transfer void under the Act, unlike a transfer made contrary to section 47(2), which section 47(3) makes void. Section 146(a) also distinguishes statutory contraventions from breaches of bye-laws. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: decree_execution_proceeding and debtor_has_right_to_occupy_society_flat and society_owns_flat and statutory_protection_covers_capital_interest_not_occupancy_right and no_absolute_transfer_bar_applies

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: A creditor is enforcing a decree against a debtor through execution proceedings.
predicates.debtor_has_right_to_occupy_society_flat: The debtor has a beneficial right to occupy a flat allotted by a cooperative housing society.
predicates.society_owns_flat: The cooperative housing society owns the flat occupied by the debtor.
predicates.statutory_protection_covers_capital_inte: The applicable statutory protection concerns a member’s share or interest in the society’s capital and does not extend to the member’s right to occupy the flat.
predicates.no_absolute_transfer_bar_applies: The governing rules do not absolutely prohibit transfer of the occupancy right, although transfer may be subject to conditions such as consent or membership requirements.

issues.definition: When a debtor’s occupancy right in a society-owned flat is being reached in decree execution and the governing law protects capital interests but does not absolutely prohibit transfer of the occupancy right, that right is attachable and saleable.

issues.legal_issue: The omission of a member’s right to occupy a cooperative housing flat from the specific property categories listed in the execution statute does not prevent attachment if the right is otherwise saleable property.
material_facts: The judgment-debtor claimed that the right to occupy the flat was not specified as attachable property in section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The Court found that the judgment-debtor had a saleable right to occupy the flat, although the flat was held in the names of his brother and his wife on his behalf.
issues.conclusion: The right to occupy the flat was attachable because section 60 is not exhaustive and includes other saleable property, including property held by another person on the judgment-debtor’s behalf.
issues.legal_principle: Section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, is not exhaustive: it extends to other saleable movable or immovable property, whether held in the judgment-debtor’s name or by another person on the judgment-debtor’s behalf. The omission of a particular species of property from its specific categories does not prevent attachment if that property is otherwise saleable. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.decree_execution_proceeding: A creditor is enforcing a decree against a debtor through execution proceedings.
predicates.debtor_has_saleable_property_interest: The debtor has an interest in property that is legally capable of being sold.
predicates.property_held_for_debtor: Another person holds the property or interest on the debtor’s behalf.

issues.definition: When a debtor has a saleable property interest in decree execution, including an interest held on the debtor’s behalf by another person, omission from specific property categories does not prevent attachment.

issues.legal_issue: A court-auction purchaser’s lack of society membership at the time of auction does not defeat attachment or sale of the occupancy right, but membership must be obtained before confirmation of the sale.
material_facts: The flat’s occupancy right was offered for sale in execution of a decree, and an auction purchaser acquired it while not a member of the society.
The transfer remained subject to the society’s membership requirements, and the sale had not been confirmed.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser’s lack of membership at the time of auction did not affect the saleability of the right or the prior attachment, but the purchaser had to obtain membership before the court confirmed the sale.
issues.legal_principle: The right to occupy a cooperative society flat may be sold in execution subject to the society’s valid membership requirements. The purchaser must obtain membership before confirmation of the sale; lack of membership at the auction does not itself invalidate the attachment or saleability. The society may refuse membership only for valid reasons. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.court_auction_of_occupancy_right: A court conducts an auction in execution to sell a debtor’s right to occupy a cooperative society flat.
predicates.purchaser_not_society_member_at_auction: The person who purchases the occupancy right at the court auction is not a member of the society when the auction occurs.

issues.definition: When a court auctions an occupancy right and the purchaser is not yet a society member, the auction sale remains permissible, subject to the purchaser obtaining membership before confirmation.
